Here is the math, including the parts that argue against buying.

mainEntity.name: How long does on-premises AI hardware last before it needs replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan on three to four years for a desktop local LLM device. The machine will still run, but newer models will outgrow its memory before its silicon wears out — so the memory ceiling, not the calendar, sets the date.

mainEntity.name: Is owning AI hardware cheaper than a per-seat subscription?

acceptedAnswer.text: At eight users, a $5,000 device with support and power costs about $19.58 per seat per month against $21 for Microsoft 365 Copilot Business. Above ten seats the owned option pulls ahead quickly because adding a user costs nothing.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my data when the hardware is replaced?

acceptedAnswer.text: It moves with you, if you planned for it. The indexed files, prompts, retrieval corpus, and evaluation set live in a directory structure you control; a refresh means copying them to the new device and re-running the evaluation.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to replace the whole device or just part of it?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a desktop device, replace the unit — component upgrades rarely pay back at that scale. For a workgroup box or rack server, memory and storage upgrades can extend life a year or two, but a GPU generation change means a new machine.

mainEntity.name: What does a local LLM device cost for a small practice?

acceptedAnswer.text: Expect roughly $4,700 to $5,500 for a capable desktop device, plus about $600 a year in support and $30 a year in electricity at Michigan commercial rates. A workgroup deployment serving a floor runs $15,000 to $40,000.
